title: PromptAndPray project config (aiwf.config.json) - v1
$comment: THE SINGLE AUTHORITY for the shape of a generated project config. scripts/setup/validate-config.mjs INTERPRETS this file; it never restates a constraint in code. The keyword subset used here is exactly the subset that interpreter supports ($schema, $id, $comment, title, description, default, type, enum, const, required, properties, additionalProperties, patternProperties, items, minItems, minLength, minimum, pattern, allOf, if, then, else) - the interpreter THROWS on any keyword it does not implement, so adding a keyword here without teaching it there fails loudly instead of being silently ignored.

$schema.description: Informational pointer at this file inside the installed plugin payload, written by /pnp:setup as an absolute path so an editor can resolve it. Nothing in the loop READS it: the authority for which payload version produced this config is _aiwf.installedPluginVersion. The path is machine-local and goes stale if the plugin root moves; that is harmless.

_aiwf.description: Bookkeeping. Written by /pnp:setup and /pnp:update ONLY - a manual edit here is a self-check failure, not a legitimate override.

installedPluginVersion.description: Semver of the plugin payload that last wrote this file. The version interlock compares the payload version against this value.

lastMigrationApplied.description: Id of the last migration whose operations are reflected in this project. A fresh install applies nothing and stamps the last entry of the payload migration manifest.

migrationJournal.description: null when no migration is in flight. Otherwise the write-ahead record of the operation being applied ({migration, opIndex, state, target, preHash, postHash, resolution}). Its exact shape is owned by the migration runner (P3) and is deliberately NOT constrained here in v1 - a schema that guesses at it would reject the runner's own journal.

managedRegions.description: One entry per managed artifact. The key is <file>#<region> for a marker region and <file> for a whole-file artifact (paths are project-relative, with forward slashes). upstream = sha256 of the content last RENDERED from the payload; local = sha256 of the content last ACCEPTED. Clean state: actual == local == upstream and override false.

override.description: true once the operator kept their own version through a conflict dialog; updates then only record the new upstream, they never apply it.

ownedAskRules.description: ONLY the ask rules setup actually INSERTED into .claude/settings.json. A desired rule that was already present is never owned and is never removed.

suppressedAskRules.description: Tombstones: owned rules the operator removed by hand. They are never forced back; only an explicit operator action clears a tombstone.

name.description: The product name, rendered into every agent file and into the managed CLAUDE.md region. No default: a project without a name is not describable to a reviewer.

description.description: One line of product description for the agent templates. Empty is legal.

stack.description: One line of stack description, e.g. "Next.js + Postgres". Empty is legal.

root.description: "auto" (resolve via `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` at Step 0) or an absolute path for a non-git edge case. NEVER render this value into a template: the render-time placeholder {{resolvedRoot}} carries the resolved path, because the literal "auto" is not one.

os.description: Selects the wrapper variant rendered into the project layer: windows -> scripts/native/ps/*.ps1, linux and macos -> scripts/native/sh/*.sh. All three channels ship wrappers; setup refuses anything outside this enum fail-closed, because an unknown channel would name wrappers that do not exist. The permission ask-ruleset is one OS-neutral superset (see templates/settings.ask-ruleset.json), not a per-OS render.

language.description: The COO <-> operator channel ONLY. Agent-to-agent traffic (briefs, verdicts) is English by doctrine and is not configurable.

roleNicknames.description: Conversational names used in the operator channel. Nothing in the filesystem, frontmatter or code is renamed with them.

roles.description: THE canonical source for roles. roles.json and the agent frontmatter are RENDERED from this block and hashed as managed artifacts; a manual edit there is a conflict, not a second source.

writer.description: The Writer is a Claude subagent by definition - it has no engine key and no external host.

model.description: Rendered into .claude/agents/writer.md frontmatter, which is the ONE place a full model id is valid (a dispatch must never pass `model`, because the Agent tool override accepts tier aliases only).

effort.$comment: see the effort note on roles.reviewer.effort

engine.description: The factory default is claude - a missing config must never fall back to a paid external engine; codex is a deliberate opt-in.

model.description: engine=claude: a TIER ALIAS only (the conditional below), because a claude-hosted role is dispatched through the Agent tool's `model` override whose enum is the aliases. engine=codex: any non-empty engine atom - the codex model vocabulary is the external engine's, and pinning it here would reject valid ids.

effort.description: Reasoning effort. Deliberately NOT an enum: the two consumers accept a free string and neither publishes a closed set to derive one from - a claude-hosted role renders it into agent frontmatter (`effort: <value>`), a codex-hosted role passes it as `-c model_reasoning_effort=<value>` to an external engine that owns its own vocabulary. The role resolver states the same contract (scripts/native/ps/aiwf-roles.ps1: engine has an enum, effort has none - a bad value is the engine's business) and rejects only a non-string or empty value, which is exactly what minLength 1 enforces here. Values seen in practice: "high", "medium".

allOf.$comment: The tier-alias conditional. Asserted independently by the self-check (tier-alias-<role>).

model.description: Same rule as roles.reviewer.model: tier alias when claude-hosted, free engine atom when codex-hosted.

effort.$comment: see the effort note on roles.reviewer.effort

qal.description: The live-browser exception. codex-only by design: the capability could not be proven on a Claude host, so no Claude QAL host exists.

enabled.description: Factory default false. /pnp:qal is fail-closed: it needs enabled=true AND engine codex AND an explicit operator request in the current conversation.

effort.$comment: see the effort note on roles.reviewer.effort

correctionRoundsCap.description: The project's VALUE for the correction-round cap. The lift gate around it (only the operator lifts it, by an explicit word, one extension at a time, recorded in the ticket's PLAN entry) is payload mechanics and is not configurable.

routeWriteGuard.description: Gate 3. true (or the key/config absent) = while .aiwf/route-state.json names an R2/R3 route, the main session may write only docs/**, .aiwf/** and root-level *.md. Only an explicit boolean false switches the route-state check off; Gate 1 (non-writer subagents cannot write) is never affected by this key.

commands.description: The project's VERIFY commands, quoted literally into every ticket brief. An empty list is legal but means briefs carry no verification track.

cwd.description: Optional, project-relative. Omitted means the project root.

e2e.description: The QA proof surface. Optional in the schema; /pnp:setup always writes the block (with enabled=false when the project has no E2E surface) so the qa agent template never renders an unresolvable path.

scratchDir.description: FIXED in v0.1: the route-state guard resolves .aiwf/route-state.json literally, so a project that moved its scratch elsewhere would arm a guard nobody writes to. The self-check asserts the same value (scratch-is-aiwf).

plansDir.description: The PARENT of active/ and archive/. A plan ENTERS the repo into <plansDir>/active/ at approval and LEAVES into <plansDir>/archive/ when every ticket is closed; setup creates both subdirectories.

overridesDoc.description: Project-relative path of the overrides document: this project's identity and hard rules. Every role reads it before starting work.

productBoundaryChecks.description: Free-text lines rendered into the reviewer agent (and the Writer's operating rules). This is where a project's product-boundary and tenancy clauses live - never in the payload. Empty is a valid answer.
